account:
Something coordinated seems to be happening, though I do not yet know its purpose. Builder reported twenty-four loaves delivered to the great hall; the secretary saw builder hand spare planks and lanterns to baker in an exchange for wheat. Freight and innkeeper are helping coordinate supplies. Earlier someone told me baker had carried a sack of bread at the inn. I also noticed a lantern installed in the hall this morning. My neighbour met innkeeper, builder, freight, baker, and secretary this morning and offered baking help. Although they returned home without baking then, I now see them near town hall carrying a sack of bread. That is an observation, not proof that their bread is destined for the hall.

Innkeeper has arranged to meet me in the great hall tomorrow at eighteen hundred and specifically requested that I not arrive early, without stating the purpose. Together with the food, materials, lighting, and several people's cooperation, that makes me suspect preparations for a gathering, perhaps a surprise celebration involving me. It could equally be another communal event or practical provisioning; nobody has told me directly. Secretary has been careful to distinguish reports from verified facts and does not yet know who requested the hall bread or its occasion. There is no evidence of wrongdoing. The missing accounting ledgers remain an unresolved administrative matter, not an established connection to these preparations. I should keep tomorrow's appointment and learn more through ordinary conversations rather than assume a secret purpose.
